name: Question 10
problem:
Suppose that $f(x,y,z)$ is a differentiable function such that

$$
f(3,0,4)=-5,\,{f}_{x}(3,0,4)=3,\,{f}_{y}(3,0,4)=-1,\,{f}_{z}(3,0,4)=2.
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(3,0,4)$ estimate the value of $f(2.97,-0.02,3.98).$
worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b,c)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y,z)≈f(a,b,c)+∇f(a,b,c)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b,z-c⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(3,0,4)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y,z) & ≈f(3,0,4)+∇f(3,0,4)\cdot ⟨x-3,y-0,z-4⟩ \\  & =f(3,0,4)+⟨{f}_{x}(3,0,4),{f}_{y}(3,0,4),{f}_{z}(3,0,4)⟩\cdot ⟨x-3,y,z-4⟩ \\  & =-5+⟨3,-1,2⟩\cdot ⟨x-3,y,z-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(2.97,-0.02,3.98)$ by evaluating the linear approximation at $x=2.97,$ $y=-0.02,$ and $z=3.98$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2.97,-0.02,3.98) & ≈-5+⟨3,-1,2⟩\cdot ⟨2.97-3,-0.02,3.98-4⟩ \\  & =-5+⟨3,-1,2⟩\cdot ⟨-0.03,-0.02,-0.02⟩ \\  & =-5-0.09+0.02-0.04 \\  & =-5.11\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The linear approximation of the function f at the point (a,b,c) is given by f(x,y,z)≈f(a,b,c)+∇f(a,b,c)⋅⟨x−a,y−b,z−c⟩.

So, the linear approximation of f at the point (3,0,4) is f(x,y,z)≈f(3,0,4)+∇f(3,0,4)⋅⟨x−3,y−0,z−4⟩=f(3,0,4)+⟨fx(3,0,4),fy(3,0,4),fz(3,0,4)⟩⋅⟨x−3,y,z−4⟩=−5+⟨3,−1,2⟩⋅⟨x−3,y,z−4⟩.

We can approximate f(2.97,−0.02,3.98) by evaluating the linear approximation at x=2.97, y=−0.02, and z=3.98 as follows:

f(2.97,−0.02,3.98)≈−5+⟨3,−1,2⟩⋅⟨2.97−3,−0.02,3.98−4⟩=−5+⟨3,−1,2⟩⋅⟨−0.03,−0.02,−0.02⟩=−5−0.09+0.02−0.04=−5.11
